searchText: for EIP-4895, does the end user (validator) still need to make some kind of a request in order to get queued for a push withdrawal to occur? other than change bls key -> eth1 address? perhaps i am not understanding how EIP-4895 works at all.... i'd have to check that eip number... ok cool... on the CL side, most validators currently have a 'withdrawal key' which is a bls key... or the nemonic for it so on the CL side they will have to change to using a eth1 address for withdrawal after that it'll just be an automated process to move funds through execution payload under a new op code that's the part i am unclear about what causes one validator index to be put into that queue for funds withdrawal ? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/capella/beacon-chain.md so current spec suggests 2 processes - partial and full.. and processed subtly differently how will that be done? basically during epoch transition full withdrawals will be added to a queue, and that queue will be drained gradually during block production i guess ultimately 'some' partials get added to that queue each epoch too will full withdrawal be a request a user must initiate manually? ahm... basically no so they will have to have eth1 address set, and have exited and waited the appropriate periods etc so they need to initiate an exit? unless slashed, they need to be in the exited state got ya so the 2 ways are slashings, or submit a voluntary exit okay, that I can understand is a voluntary exit an EL transaction with gas costs? voluntary exit is on the CL side, no gas okay afaik at least i think you're right, I haven't looked at it deeply what about partial withdrawals? how will those be dequeued? who gets it first? or is it random for any validator index above 32ETH? i mean i know its on the CL, and there was no gas mechanism for it when we wrote it, i cant imagine that'd change so the spec is basically process up to 256 per epoch ,and keep a counter of where we get to, so it's like a sweep over a number of epochs and literally anything over 32 eth gets drained and given back (if eth1address set) at 256 per epoch, people likely to get a deposit every couple of weeks roughly is it just an incremental counter starting from 0 representing the validator index? or is it randomized? increment start from 0 round robbin okay understood and one final question if you don't mind sure 🙂 how does one set their eth1 address? thats a good question 🙂 there's a process in the spec to set it, but im not sure whether clients will each implement a CLI, or if it should belong somewhere else... a lot of people will want to submit a nemonic and set their eth1address, so it may need more tooling than a lot of clients support currently it's also a 1-shot kinda deal - so people will need to be super careful is that going to be an execution layer operation or similarly to an exit, a CL operation ? the CL will need ot process the command to update the validator in the state, the EL won't need to be aware of that detail so it'll be like 16 per block currently to make that change, and clients will likely need to gossip and keep a queue, i think the constant is `MAX_BLS_TO_EXECUTION_CHANGES` 16 such updates per block? so you're looking at a waiting time until your update gets solidifed? yeh it'll process fast, but its limited by the number allowed per block got ya full block inclusion would be 512 / epoch i seem to remember some talk of a possible mechanism to help those that got their validator mnemonic exposed... is there anything like that still being talked about or is that impossible? i haven't seen anything concrete, but yes i'd be concerned if i was in that bucket yeah not the best bucket to be in for sure i was just curious if this is still a race to get your operation before the hacker also a hard problem, i'm not sure if anyone is specifically investigating that... we've been mostly in the weeds looking at the implementation details i can imagine, you guys don't really have a lack of problems to tackle and its all very much appreciated thanks 🙂 is the eth1 address set going to be the same one used for the exit operation? one address for both partial and full yep - and it can't execute EVM code when using that new op code, so that's probably worth being aware of its a free op, so won't cost gas, but also restricted from running EVM... not sure the implications because i'm on the CL side, but it does sound important to know yes it does indeed are partial and full both currently slated for finding themselves into Shanghai or is only one of the two for now going to make it? it's the 1 op from the EL side, so it'll just be what gets put into that list... currently both are slated for the same release on the CL side i understand thank you very much for answering all of these questions! really really appreciate it! very welcome 🙂 hope you have a nice rest of your day! you too thanks! <@199561711278227457> how can I run locally all of the CI for a spec-repo PR so that I stop spamming the CI runner? Ah I think I got all CI but spectests passing. I won't fix tests unless that's the PR we're going with

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: for EIP-4895, does the end user (validator) still need to make some kind of a request in order to get queued for a push withdrawal to occur?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: other than change bls key -> eth1 address?

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: perhaps i am not understanding how EIP-4895 works at all....

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: i'd have to check that eip number...

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: ok cool... on the CL side, most validators currently have a 'withdrawal key' which is a bls key...

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: or the nemonic for it

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: so on the CL side they will have to change to using a eth1 address for withdrawal

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: after that it'll just be an automated process to move funds through execution payload under a new op code

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: that's the part i am unclear about

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: what causes one validator index to be put into that queue for funds withdrawal ?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/capella/beacon-chain.md
so current spec suggests 2 processes - partial and full.. and processed subtly differently

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: how will that be done?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: basically during epoch transition full withdrawals will be added to a queue, and that queue will be drained gradually during block production

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: i guess ultimately 'some' partials get added to that queue each epoch too

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: will full withdrawal be a request a user must initiate manually?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: ahm... basically no

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: so they will have to have eth1 address set, and have exited

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: and waited the appropriate periods etc

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: so they need to initiate an exit?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: unless slashed, they need to be in the exited state

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: got ya

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: so the 2 ways are slashings, or submit a voluntary exit

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: okay, that I can understand

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: is a voluntary exit an EL transaction with gas costs?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: voluntary exit is on the CL side, no gas

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: okay

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: afaik at least

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: i think you're right, I haven't looked at it deeply

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: what about partial withdrawals? how will those be dequeued? who gets it first? or is it random for any validator index above 32ETH?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: i mean i know its on the CL, and there was no gas mechanism for it when we wrote it, i cant imagine that'd change

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: so the spec is basically process up to 256 per epoch ,and keep a counter of where we get to, so it's like a sweep over a number of epochs

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: and literally anything over 32 eth gets drained and given back (if eth1address set)

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: at 256 per epoch, people likely to get a deposit every couple of weeks roughly

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: is it just an incremental counter starting from 0 representing the validator index? or is it randomized?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: increment start from 0

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: round robbin

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: okay understood

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: and one final question if you don't mind

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: sure 🙂

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: how does one set their eth1 address?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: thats a good question 🙂

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: there's a process in the spec to set it, but im not sure whether clients will each implement a CLI, or if it should belong somewhere else... a lot of people will want to submit a nemonic and set their eth1address, so it may need more tooling than a lot of clients support currently

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: it's also a 1-shot kinda deal - so people will need to be super careful

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: is that going to be an execution layer operation or similarly to an exit, a CL operation ?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: the CL will need ot process the command to update the validator in the state, the EL won't need to be aware of that detail

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: so it'll be like 16 per block currently to make that change, and clients will likely need to gossip and keep a queue, i think

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: the constant is `MAX_BLS_TO_EXECUTION_CHANGES`

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: 16 such updates per block? so you're looking at a waiting time until your update gets solidifed?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: yeh it'll process fast, but its limited by the number allowed per block

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: got ya

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: full block inclusion would be 512 / epoch

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: i seem to remember some talk of a possible mechanism to help those that got their validator mnemonic exposed... is there anything like that still being talked about or is that impossible?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: i haven't seen anything concrete, but yes i'd be concerned if i was in that bucket

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: yeah not the best bucket to be in for sure

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: i was just curious if this is still a race to get your operation before the hacker

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: also a hard problem, i'm not sure if anyone is specifically investigating that... we've been mostly in the weeds looking at the implementation details

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: i can imagine, you guys don't really have a lack of problems to tackle

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: and its all very much appreciated

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: thanks 🙂

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: is the eth1 address set going to be the same one used for the exit operation?

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: one address for both partial and full

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: yep - and it can't execute EVM code when using that new op code, so that's probably worth being aware of

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: its a free op, so won't cost gas, but also restricted from running EVM... not sure the implications because i'm on the CL side, but it does sound important to know

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: yes it does indeed

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: are partial and full both currently slated for finding themselves into Shanghai or is only one of the two for now going to make it?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: it's the 1 op from the EL side, so it'll just be what gets put into that list... currently both are slated for the same release on the CL side

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: i understand

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: thank you very much for answering all of these questions! really really appreciate it!

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: very welcome 🙂

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: hope you have a nice rest of your day!

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: you too

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content: thanks!
